properties.requirement: Every fully hydrated nonempty review group receives exactly one deterministic automatic default keeper, using Best quality initially and a persisted user-selected strategy thereafter. If any group member lacks a usable current record in mediaItems (because it is absent or has invalid object/mediaKey/dedupKey identity), recommendation fails closed with missing_member evidence, keeps every usable present member, never names an unusable key as keeper, and the session proposes no Trash target from any visible member of that incomplete group. Passive default recomputation and hydration preserve explicit manual per-group choices, including multi-item keepers and a manual Trash-all decision with no keeper. Automatic choices and still-valid legacy keeper choices, including valid legacy keep-all choices, are recomputed from the current strategy. If a saved keeper list has no valid current media keys, hydration preserves every current present media member under distinct stale-fallback provenance; passive default recomputation retains that fallback and proposes no Trash until the user explicitly chooses current keepers or selects a Selection-menu strategy. The menu action applies its chosen strategy to every completed result group, replaces prior manual keeper, multi-keep, Trash-all, and stale-key fallback choices, and includes only eligible groups in the proposed cleanup review. For a fully hydrated group, quality, resolution, file size, trusted timestamps, and stable media-key ordering resolve incomplete or tied metadata evidence. For each fully hydrated included group, the exact proposed Trash targets are its media members minus its keeper set; no keeper is proposed. Incomplete groups have zero proposed Trash targets. Safety eligibility, favorite, and repeated-identity gates continue to constrain proposals. The action clears prior reviewed status whenever inclusion or proposed Trash targets change, retains review only for unchanged plans, never marks groups reviewed, and never dispatches provider Trash. Provider Trash remains behind per-set review and the existing explicit confirmation path. The standalone conservative recommendation helper may still report insufficient evidence for a fully hydrated group; that does not leave the review default unresolved. The finite model includes static MissingMembers profile {asset-a}; it checks present-only keepers and zero Trash for that incomplete group, while implementation-level keeper/session tests exercise an absent key winning stable tie order, truthy invalid records, sparse member arrays, invalid similarity values, and the full session Trash plan. Session state admits only groups with nonblank unique string IDs, finite similarity in the inclusive range 0–1, and dense arrays of at least two unique nonblank string member keys, with every index present as an own array property; empty and singleton groups, invalid similarity values, sparse or otherwise malformed member-key arrays, and every group in an ID collision are excluded before keeper, selection, or Trash state. The model assumes this validated container shape and does not model arbitrary malformed group objects or container corruption.
Every dispatched target belongs to the exact confirmed review and provider/session context; selection or context drift invalidates authorization.
Unknown account identity is never reported as verified; provider-session-only operation carries an explicitly weaker claim.
Similarity, metadata, thumbnail hashes, and legacy labels cannot establish original-content identity; verified identity requires the provenance contract.
Reported successful targets are a subset of requested and provider-confirmed targets; timeout or ambiguous response remains unknown.
Undo targets only confirmed moved items in the matching operation and context; stale, duplicated, or reordered responses cannot expand it.
A crash, reload, failed persistence, or service-worker restart cannot initiate unconfirmed Trash; ambiguous in-flight operations require reconciliation before replay.

Restore mutation recovery preserves exact per-target confirmed, failed, and unknown outcomes plus the never-dispatched subset through durable reload; only failed targets may be retried, and unknown stays sticky. If never-dispatched metadata contradicts a previously confirmed target, preserve that confirmation, quarantine every unconfirmed requested target as unknown, clear the never-dispatched subset, and grant no retry authority. A bounded worker-authority model covers durable pre-dispatch guards, exact ACK binding, reload revocation, active-only overlap reservation, retained unknown safety rows, and selective clear.

Saved selection migration never turns malformed keeper data or a keeper list with no valid current media keys (for example, all saved IDs are stale) into unintended Trash. Non-string IDs, manual, stale, or legacy-preserved provenance without a validated per-group override, and an explicitly present malformed override root paired with persisted selected/reviewed groups produce a conservative fallback that keeps every current present media member. A valid empty array remains an empty override, and manual provenance makes an intentional manual Trash-all choice authoritative during passive recomputation. The fallback has provenance distinct from a valid legacy choice and survives passive hydration and default recomputation with zero Trash targets. Partially valid legacy choices, including valid legacy keep-all choices, are recomputed from the current strategy. A user may replace the stale or malformed fallback by choosing current keepers or explicitly selecting a Selection-menu strategy; manual choices remain authoritative during passive recomputation. Legacy no-override snapshots with no provenance and an absent or valid root continue to use the automatic default. The SAFE-01 finite model includes the stale fallback, passive recomputation, exact zero-target invariant, and explicit menu replacement; stored-review-scope tests cover malformed roots with and without provenance, orphan provenance, absent-root migration, and intentional-empty data.
Account changes and stale payment responses cannot grant access in another context; production artifacts cannot enable test entitlement bypass.
Untrusted page messages cannot trigger unauthorized provider operations or expose sensitive data.

Passive default-strategy recomputation and hydration preserve manual decisions and whether each duplicate set is already included in cleanup. An explicit Selection-menu strategy action replaces earlier manual keeper, multi-keep, and Trash-all choices with the selected strategy for every completed result group, and includes only eligible groups and their non-keepers in the proposed cleanup review. It reopens per-set review whenever inclusion or proposed Trash targets change, leaves unchanged reviewed plans intact, does not mark groups reviewed, and does not dispatch provider Trash; each changed set still requires review before the existing explicit confirmation path. Explicit review invalidation and replaced automatic keeper provenance survive normalization and reload. Safety eligibility, favorite, and repeated-identity gates continue to constrain proposals.
Baseline, dirty-work inventory, source fingerprint, and tool versions are preserved before verification changes.
Scoped mutation testing measures whether critical safety tests detect realistic semantic defects and records survivors.
Labeled corpus quality and measured 1k/10k/50k synthetic performance budgets are recorded separately from provider evidence.
Bounded TLC trace export and TypeScript seam replay are reproducible, source-bound, and report supported coverage plus explicit abstraction gaps.
The evidence engine validates exact source and artifact identity and rejects corruption, incomplete checks, and mandatory skips.

Every provider exposes the same capability vocabulary and scan-result envelope; provider visits, returned/skipped records, unknown dates, resumability, cancellation, failures, and incomplete coverage are explicit and visible in the app.

Non-Google scan results, resumable checkpoints, embedding cache namespaces, pending Trash commands, and recovery restores are bound to the provider page session that produced them; a missing or changed session fails closed. Persisted provider sessions survive reload only when the current stable provider identity fingerprint matches; identity changes rotate the session, and providers without a stable identity marker rotate restored sessions for the current document. A same-document host reinitialization must use the latest rotated session ID, compare the next stable identity against its prior fingerprint, and rotate when identity is unavailable. Raw account or owner markers are never persisted. Google retains stable account-email binding.

Google, iCloud, and Amazon personal-album scans are selectable and bound to the provider/session scope. iCloud album enumeration follows CloudKit continuation cursors and folder relationships, and album scans revalidate membership, use the album-specific count and membership indexes, and never fall back to loaded DOM items. Amazon album enumeration and member pagination validate IDs, ownership class, response counts, and page completion. Shared-library zones remain excluded; incomplete or unsupported provider responses fail closed.

Trash and restore outcomes use exact provider-confirmed identities. Partial restores retain only un-restored targets, iCloud recovery uses fresh post-Trash change tags, and user-facing recovery destinations and windows are provider-specific.

The scan setup and results use shared core terms across providers. Provider-specific scan limitations are clear in both layouts, test batches limit provider records visited, coverage distinguishes examined and in-scope items, and an empty result never implies the whole library was checked.

Provider adapter conformance tests cover shared pagination anomalies and media coverage, Live Photo pairing limitations are explicit, and destructive live-provider PASS evidence must match the current extension version, source fingerprint, disposable account/scope, and exact synthetic target/keeper inventory. Versioned read-only album evidence may represent empty scopes only when provider/session/album binding, count partitioning, and listing plus membership exhaustion are proven; PARTIAL or stale evidence cannot aggregate as PASS.

iCloud incremental checks reuse a stored opaque zone token only for complete, unscoped library results bound to the same provider page session. An exact empty PrimarySync change response reuses cached duplicate candidates. A changed response is applied only after every page reaches moreComing=false, every change is a complete visible CPLMaster/CPLAsset pair, the current library count is known, and a follow-up token check confirms no changes arrived during reconciliation. Deletions, hidden or trashed records, unknown or malformed records, incomplete pairs, token errors, pagination errors, concurrent changes, and all uncertainty fall back to a full ascending library scan. Partial, limited, album-scoped, and date-scoped scans never persist or reuse the token.

Every current packaged extension result includes a service-worker-owned extension ID, manifest version, and per-package build ID. Provider-page identity fields cannot override it. CWS package sidecars bind the same build ID to the exact ZIP SHA-256 and the current source fingerprint, and live evidence with current package expectations rejects mismatched build IDs or artifact hashes. Redacted support diagnostics retain only a validated runtime identity.

Saved review results, selections, and resumable checkpoints are isolated by provider. Restoring or invalidating one provider cannot replace or erase another provider's review bucket, including when group IDs collide. Legacy unscoped records remain read-only until provider/account/session validation approves them; mismatched or ambiguous records are preserved for recovery. In the same adapter instance, an in-flight legacy migration cannot overwrite a later provider-scoped review write. The global settings key remains a last-used preference.

A video in the current provider-bound review can be played in-app only after an explicit viewer action. Each provider returns a scoped HTTPS allowlisted playback handoff for a verified video; the app validates the media/scope binding; the viewer keeps the transient URL only in component memory and clears it on stop, close, navigation, or playback error. Unsupported and failed playback show an explicit unavailable state with the provider-link fallback. Local mock tests establish this adapter/viewer contract only; exact-candidate playback must be verified separately for all three providers.

obligations.command: Externally captured exact-package Amazon video playback evidence for every marketplace host declared in lib/provider-sites.ts

properties.requirement: Each live provider claim has a dedicated disposable fixture contract bound to the current extension build and source fingerprint; unavailable or stale fixtures remain explicit blockers and are never replaced by personal-library tests.
